messages:
jess: Quick heads-up — during the private CP peering spike I hit a routing asymmetry when customer VPCs use /28 egress pools. Packets from our control plane SNAT to an ephemeral IP in AZ-A, but return traffic gets routed to a different ENI in AZ-B and is dropped. Short thread with options below.

ali: TL;DR — is this NAT exhaustion or route visibility?

jess: It's a mix. We SNAT from TGW -> shared /28 (per-region pool). Customer replies use route propagation that prefers an ENI in another AZ (different source IP mapping). No connection tracking across that path.

mario: Oof. That sounds like ephemeral SNAT + per-AZ route convergence = broken TCP flows. How often does it hit?

jess: Repro about 1/1000 requests in our sim harness, higher with bursty onboarding traffic. Seen mainly on long-lived TLS sessions and streaming RPCs.

kendra: Possible mitigations: 1) Per-customer static ENI/NAT allocation (preserve srcip), 2) Use PrivateLink (NLB) so replies follow same AZ, 3) Add return-route programming on customer route tables (ugh ops), 4) Proxy at the edge (TLS termination/proxy protocol). Tradeoffs: cost, IP pressure, ops complexity.

ali: Can we avoid changing customer infra? We should prefer solutions that don't require manual customer RT edits.

jess: Agreed. That makes PrivateLink or per-customer ENI/NAT the top candidates. PrivateLink buys stable pathing but has scaling and regional endpoint lifecycle considerations. Per-customer ENI/NAT is simple conceptually but we run out of IPs fast and adds infra to manage.

mario: Also consider a short-term hack: maintain a mapping table in the edge layer so we SNAT from a pinned IP for active connections for N minutes. Less IP pressure than static ENI. Fallback to shared pool for new flows.

kendra: That mapping idea could be lower risk: allocate a small sticky IP pool, track 5m-15m sticky affinity, and evict least-recently-used. Needs observability.

jess: Implementation sketch: sticky map keyed by customerID + srcport range. On egress, if entry exists use pinned ip; otherwise allocate sticky ip if below threshold, else use shared pool. Fallback policy to drop into shared pool when sticky allocation fails.

deploy-bot: test/deploy pipeline: pushed branch cp/sticky-snat to staging, running integ tests.

ali: What about security & trust surface? PrivateLink isolates CP endpoints but requires certs + mTLS as usual. Sticky SNAT keeps current trust model.

mario: Cost estimate quick take: per-customer ENI ~= $X/day per tenant; PrivateLink VPC endpoint scales with connections and ENI count per AZ; sticky SNAT mostly engineering time + small reserved IP pool.

kendra: Also think about DNS split-horizon. PrivateLink would let us serve private CP DNS that resolves to endpoints per-region; sticky SNAT doesn't solve split-horizon cert selection for some customers.

jess: Action items:
- short-term: implement sticky SNAT prototype in edge runtime and enable for 10 pilot customers (owner: jess)
- medium-term: evaluate PrivateLink for high-security customers (owner: kendra)
- long-term: quantify IP cost and automation for per-customer ENI (owner: mario)

jess: I'll open an RFC follow-up with the prototype plan and a small observability dashboard request (flows stuck, SNAT hits, evictions). Assigning a small risk window for rollout.

ali: Thanks — add me as reviewer on the RFC. Also add a metric for TLS session resets.

jess: Will do. :thumbsup:
